paper.title_en: Affine ANEC selects the closed FRW branch for geodesically complete cosmology
paper.abstract_en: Using the affinely parameterized averaged null energy condition (ANEC) along radial null geodesics, we prove that, within the globally nondegenerate Friedmann--Robertson--Walker (FRW) class with $a(t)>0$ for all cosmic times, non-static flat models and all open models cannot be both null geodesically complete and ANEC-satisfying. Bounded oscillatory or cyclic flat/open models obey the same obstruction; in non-static periodic cases the negative affine-ANEC contribution accumulates over infinitely many cycles, giving $I_{\rm ANEC}=-\infty$. The sign obstruction is absent in closed $(k=+1)$ FRW geometry, where positive curvature can offset the negative expansion contribution to the affine ANEC, allowing nonsingular, geodesically complete cosmologies with ordinary NEC-respecting matter. We construct closed-FRW scalar-field models and contrast them with their flat realizations, which require NEC-violating support. We show that neglecting small positive curvature in a flat reconstruction of the expansion history can produce an apparent phantom equation of state, with a percent-level shift at $z=1$. Our main result is a curvature classification of ANEC-compatible eternal FRW cosmologies within this class: non-static flat and all open models are obstructed, while the closed branch admits explicit complete realizations, with global de Sitter as the vacuum representative.
